description: Believes textContent or createTextNode parses injected markup into live HTML elements, rather than storing it as inert text.
Believes a script tag inserted via innerHTML executes, when HTML-parsed script elements inserted this way do not run (though event-handler attributes still do).
Believes insertAdjacentHTML is a safe sink that does not create live elements from untrusted strings.
Believes assigning untrusted input to el.className can inject HTML elements, confusing attribute-value assignment with markup parsing.
Believes stripping script tags with a regex sanitizes HTML, ignoring nested-fragment bypasses and inline handlers like onerror on other elements.
Believes the order of HTML escape replacements does not matter, missing that escaping & after < double-encodes entities or leaves gaps.
Believes escaping only some characters (e.g. < and &, not > or quotes) is enough to make output safe in every HTML context.
Believes window.name, document.referrer, or location.hash are trustworthy inputs rather than attacker-controllable DOM XSS sources.
Believes decoding a URL fragment strips or neutralizes tags, when it only converts percent escapes back into dangerous characters.
Believes javascript: is not a valid URL scheme, so URL parsing or anchor href assignment rejects it or reports a different protocol.
Believes a scheme allowlist check on the parsed protocol would let javascript: URLs through, or that missing validation is harmless.
Believes url.startsWith(allowedOrigin) validates the host, missing that https://example.com.evil.net shares the prefix.
Believes url.endsWith('.example.com') proves the host belongs to example.com, ignoring paths or queries that end with the suffix.
Believes href.includes('https://example.com') shows a URL points at example.com, even when it appears in a query parameter.
Believes https://example.com@evil.com has hostname example.com, missing that the part before @ is credentials and the host is evil.com.
Believes any target starting with '/' is a same-site path, missing that '//evil.com' is protocol-relative and switches the host.
Believes a backslash in a URL path is an ordinary character, missing that parsers normalize /\evil.com into //evil.com and change the authority.
Confuses URL host, hostname, origin, and default ports: believes hostname includes the port, origin includes the path, or :443 appears in https origins.
Believes event.origin or an origin includes the path or query, or that an explicit default port makes origin strings differ from the canonical form.
Believes postMessage with targetOrigin '*' delivers only to the intended page, or that a host pattern like *.example.com is a valid targetOrigin.
Believes functions can be sent via postMessage or structuredClone, when the structured clone algorithm throws DataCloneError for them.
Believes subdomains or other schemes and ports are the same origin as the parent domain, ignoring that scheme, host, and port must all match.
Believes a recursive merge of parsed JSON cannot affect other objects, missing that a __proto__ key can write onto Object.prototype.
Believes JSON.parse treats a '__proto__' key as setting the prototype, when it creates a plain own property with that name.
Believes prototype pollution also affects Object.create(null) objects, Map lookups, or getAttribute, which do not consult Object.prototype.
Believes the 'in' operator or truthiness checks only see own properties, missing that inherited polluted keys are visible and hasOwn is needed.
Believes writing to a frozen Object.prototype always throws, when sloppy-mode scripts fail silently and only strict mode raises TypeError.
Believes CSP directives without an explicit entry are unrestricted, missing that fetch directives fall back to default-src (but frame-ancestors does not).
Believes frame-ancestors falls back to default-src or that frame-src or child-src controls who may embed the page.
Believes unsafe-inline still allows nonce-less inline scripts when a nonce is present, or that unsafe-inline also governs eval, which needs unsafe-eval.
Believes CSP host sources match loosely, e.g. *.example.com matching the bare domain or lookalike hosts, or an https source matching http.
Believes 'self' in a CSP also covers other origins such as a CDN host or sibling subdomain.
Believes the Secure or SameSite attribute hides a cookie from document.cookie, when only HttpOnly does so.
Believes document.cookie returns the cookie attributes such as Path and Max-Age, when it exposes only name=value pairs.
Believes SameSite=None cookies are accepted without the Secure attribute, or that Lax or Strict permit cross-site subresource requests.
Believes cookie Path matching is a plain string prefix, so /app also matches /apple, or that Path acts as a security boundary.
Believes Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * permits credentialed cross-origin requests, or that simple GETs and text/plain POSTs trigger preflights.
Believes X-Frame-Options works when set in a meta tag or that ALLOW-FROM is honored by modern browsers, when both are ignored.
Believes iframe sandbox grants capabilities by default or that allow-scripts implies allow-same-origin, forms, or popups, when each needs its own token.
